newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Bank Handlowy sees flat 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Bank Handlowy sees flat 1997 earnings.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy SA, earmarked for privatisation this year, expects its earnings to stay flat in 1997 after an exceptionally good performance last year, the bank's president said on Wednesday.
"We expect our net 1997 profit to be roughly the same as in 1996, which was an exceptionally good result," Cezary Stypulkowski told Reuters in an interview.
Stypulkowski said that according to preliminary results Bank Handlowy earned net 555 million zlotys in 1996 up from 425 million in 1995.
The strong net earnings growth was in part possible because the bank was able to reduce bad debt provisions thanks to an improved credit portfolio.
Stypulkowski said the bank should also maintain the real value of shareholder equity or even improve capital strength to more than two billion zlotys from the current 1.85 billion.
"I believe that we will maintain the real value of our own assets or even increase it," he added.
He said that thanks to a sufficiently high capital the bank would be able to offer a 25-percent dividend for 1996.
"The 1996 dividend will be substantially higher than last year and the management plans to propose a 25-percent pay-out ratio," Stypulkowski said.

According to preliminary figures, at the end of 1996 Bank Handlowy had a balance sheet total of 13.31 billion zlotys, up 51.3 percent from 1995. Handlowy's financial director Witold Walkowiak told Reuters the balance sheet total might substantially increase.
It recorded a pre-tax profit of 770.8 million zlotys against 731 million in 1995.
